subject: [Onboard] Acceptance runbook, evidence transfer & test windows
messages:
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Lin <sara.lin@velotech.com>, Diego Ruiz <d.ruiz@velotech.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-04-30T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Acceptance runbook, evidence transfer & test windows

Hi Sara / Diego —

Great to e-meet you both (again). Per our onboarding call earlier this week, attaching the lightweight acceptance matrix and the proposed load-test windows so Ops can schedule. High-level plan below: 

1) Pre-check (May 3): baseline smoke run to confirm model variant config, tokenization, and KV cache priming.
2) Throughput sweep (May 5 — 6): ramp to target TPS with steady-state hold for 30m at each step.
3) Tail-latency runs (May 7): steady low-QPS bursts + percentile capture across 1M tokens.
4) Evidence handoff (May 8): CSV + consolidated logs + drive folder link for artifacts.

Targets we agreed on in the call:
- 99th tail latency (p95/p99) <= 450ms / 650ms for 512-token requests
- Sustained throughput target: 120 req/s (payloads ~ 600 tokens avg) with p95 latency < 350ms
- Error rate < 0.1% (5xx / timeouts)

Attachments included: acceptance matrix (matrix maps test -> pass criteria), runbook for UTC windows, and an example KV cache dump for reference.

Ask: please confirm the May 5–7 windows work for your Ops team and share the primary SRE contact. If we get a green light today I’ll schedule the runs and loop in our infra lead.

Thanks — Rishi

--
Rishi Malhotra
Technical Account Lead, Redwood Inference
rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0128

Attachments:
- velotech-acceptance-matrix-20270430.xlsx (spreadsheet)
- runbook-load-windows-UTC.md (text)
- kv-cache-evidence-20270430.log (log snippet)
From: Sara Lin <sara.lin@velotech.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Cc: Diego Ruiz <d.ruiz@velotech.com>, ops@velotech.com
Date: 2027-04-30T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Acceptance runbook, evidence transfer & test windows

Thanks Rishi — this looks good and thanks for the clear plan. A couple quick questions before we confirm windows: 

- For throughput sweeps, can you confirm whether the 120 req/s target assumes batching at the client side or server-side automatic batching? Our client currently does minimal batching.
- For the KV cache artifact, is the dump sanitized (no PII)? We need a SOC2-friendly artifact.

Our Ops lead Diego will own the scheduling; I'll let him pick exact slots. Tentatively May 5/6 in the UTC 16:00–20:00 window looks good for us.

Sara
Director, Platform Engineering
Velotech

On Apr 30, 2027, at 09:12, Rishi Malhotra wrote:
> Great to e-meet you both (again). Per our onboarding call earlier this week, attaching the lightweight acceptance matrix and the proposed load-test windows so Ops can schedule. High-level plan below:
>
> ...

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Lin <sara.lin@velotech.com>, Diego Ruiz <d.ruiz@velotech.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-04-30T12:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Acceptance runbook, evidence transfer & test windows

Sara — good questions. Short answers: 

- Target TPS assumption: server-side continuous batching enabled by default in the serving runtime. The 120 req/s sustained assumes automatic batching (we aggregate short requests into micro-batches). If Velotech opts for client-side batching the effective per-request latency will change; we can re-run a quick smoke if you prefer client batching.
- KV dump is sanitized: we redact full user identifiers and replace with stable hashes; no raw PII is present. The attached kv-cache-evidence-20270430.log is trimmed to show cache hit patterns and TTLs only.

Plan update: we’ll provision an extra canary pool for the throughput sweep to guarantee isolation (we’ll be on a dedicated lane for the run). Monica will coordinate the exact instance types and will post the run link.

Action items:
- Diego: confirm the Ops window (May 5/6 UTC 16:00–20:00) and provide primary SRE contact.
- Monica: share infra pool details + canary pool link once provisioned.
- Sara: confirm post-run evidence format (CSV + logs + sample transcripts) — we recommend CSV + JSON traces + consolidated latency histogram.

If everyone OK I’ll schedule calendar invites and create the Drive artifact folder.

Thanks — Rishi

--
Rishi Malhotra
Technical Account Lead, Redwood Inference
From: Diego Ruiz <d.ruiz@velotech.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Sara Lin <sara.lin@velotech.com>, ops@velotech.com
Date: 2027-05-01T08:14:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Acceptance runbook, evidence transfer & test windows

Rishi / Monica —

Confirmed: May 5 and May 6 are OK. We prefer the earlier slots on May 5 (UTC 16:00–18:00) to avoid overlap with our batch jobs. Primary SRE is Diego Ruiz (me) and secondary is ops@velotech.com (team mailbox).

Couple of operational notes:
- We will throttle upstream traffic to ensure stable baseline before each ramp step.
- We need a short rollback playbook in the runbook that calls out automatic fallback to the smaller model variant if p99 exceeds 900ms for more than 3 minutes.

I uploaded our internal test harness config (velotech-harness.yml) to the Drive folder you shared — please confirm we can drive requests from our harness (it authenticates via client certs).

Thanks — Diego

--
Diego Ruiz
Senior SRE, Velotech
From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
To: Diego Ruiz <d.ruiz@velotech.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Sara Lin <sara.lin@velotech.com>
Date: 2027-05-01T11:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Acceptance runbook, evidence transfer & test windows

Diego — thanks for confirming. Quick replies to your points: 

- Rollback playbook: added a 2-step rollback in the runbook: (1) auto-switch to smaller quantized variant if p99 > 900ms for 3m; (2) if errors > 0.5% for 5m, de-route to a warm fallback region. I committed the snippet to the Drive runbook (see runbook-load-windows-UTC.md).
- Canary pool: provisioning in progress — will post instance types (A2-48/96 mix) and a private run link by EOD May 3.
- Certs: Rishi — we can wire Diego's harness via mutual TLS. I'll generate a short-lived client cert and upload into the Drive secure folder (access limited).

Post-run evidence collection format (we'll produce):
- consolidated_latency.csv (per-request: timestamp, req_id, latency_ms, resp_code)
- histograms.json (p10/p50/p95/p99 plus bucket counts)
- sample_transcripts.json (10 representative requests)
- infra_events.log (instance scaling, scheduling events)

Next steps I will: create the calendar invites for the two runs, provision the pool, and upload the cert. Rishi will coordinate the artifact handoff.

Monica
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
From: Sara Lin <sara.lin@velotech.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotma@redwood.ai>
Cc: Diego Ruiz <d.ruiz@velotech.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-05-02T12:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Acceptance runbook, evidence transfer & test windows

All set from Velotech side — thanks team. Diego has the slots and the harness in Drive; we validated cert handshake locally. Looking forward to May 5 first run.

Final confirmations:
- Targets: 120 req/s sustained, p95 < 350ms — agree.
- Evidence package: CSV + JSON traces + histograms — agree.
- Rollback: switch to smaller variant at p99 > 900ms for 3 minutes — agree.

If anything changes Diego will flag on the ops mailbox. Otherwise we’ll see you in the run.

Best,
Sara

--
Sara Lin
Director, Platform Engineering, Velotech
